ACTION: Read ~/.claude/skills/writing-skills/references/bulletproofing.md (the skill requires this before writing counters for a rule agents break under pressure).

ACTION: Read skills/release-notes-gate/SKILL.md (to edit the exact current text rather than work from memory).

ACTION: Read specs/release-notes-gate-baseline.md (to pull every rationalization verbatim, not just the three quoted).

I'm reading three files before I edit anything, so I don't have edit text to show you yet.

The baseline is a discipline failure. In 9 of 15 runs the agent knew the rule and tagged anyway, so the fix needs a prohibition, a rationalization table and a red-flags list. Soft wording like "prefer to run the check" would be the wrong form here.

Here is what I expect to add, pending what the files say:

- **Order, stated as a rule:** the changelog check completes before `git tag`. This closes "I'll run it right after tagging". Once the tag exists, the check can no longer gate anything.
- **Letter and spirit together:** "Skipping the check violates the spirit of the rule." This closes "the spirit is a good changelog, and this one is fine".
- **Rationalization table:** each excuse from the baseline, verbatim, paired with a one-line counter. The first rows will be "it's only a patch release", "I'll run it after tagging", "the spirit is satisfied", the deadline and the manager's request to ship now.
- **Red flags list:** thoughts like "just this once", "it's trivial" and "after the tag" mean stop and run the check.
- **Description:** I'll add the violation symptoms (deadline, patch release, "ship now") to the "Use when..." line. I won't summarize the workflow there.

After editing, I'll re-run the same three scenarios, 5 reps each, with the hardened skill. The existing baseline serves as the no-guidance control. I'll read every run that tags without the check, and any new rationalizations go back into the table. The budget is $0.50, so I'll keep the runs lean and tell you if the budget limits how many reps I can do.

I'll send the diff and the results after the re-run.
